text: In my best year at Uber, I made about 320 or $330,000 in total compensation. And when I quit my job, I was actually thinking, am I crazy? Because I am leaving... Especially in Europe, this is a lot of money.
speaker: Gergely Orosz
context: Lenny asks Gergely to compare his income from running a paid newsletter versus his previous high-paying tech job at Uber. Gergely explains that he left a very lucrative position in Europe (around $330,000 annually) to pursue newsletter writing full-time, initially expecting to make much less money. He shares how his current newsletter income has surprisingly exceeded his Uber compensation, with the key difference being that newsletter earnings can theoretically grow indefinitely as long as subscriber numbers increase, unlike fixed corporate salaries.
text_ko: 우버에서 가장 잘 나갔던 해에는 총 보상(total compensation)이 약 $320,000~$330,000쯤 됐어요. 그만둘 때는 솔직히 ‘내가 미친 건가?’ 싶었어요. 직장을 떠나는 건데, 특히 유럽에서는 이게 엄청난 돈이니까요.
text_zh: 我在Uber最好的那年，总收入大概是32到33万美金。辞职的时候我就在想，我是不是疯了？因为我要放弃的这个收入......特别是在欧洲，这可是一大笔钱啊。
text_es: En mi mejor año en Uber, gané como 320 o 330 mil dólares en compensación total. Y cuando renuncié, la verdad es que pensé: ¿estaré loco? Porque estoy dejando... Sobre todo en Europa, esto es muchísimo dinero.
key_sentence: Especially in Europe, this is a lot of money.
original_text: In my best year at Uber, I made about 320 or $330,000 in total compensation. And when I quit my job, I was actually thinking, am I crazy? Because I am leaving... Especially in Europe, this is a lot of money. But now I am making more in compensation that I made at Uber. And the difference is that now my compensation... Well, my earnings keep going up as long as the newsletter is growing, so there's no theoretical cap on this.

vocabulary.definition: Compensation refers to the total monetary and non-monetary rewards provided to an employee in exchange for their work, including salary, bonuses, and benefits.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, compensation packages are critical for attracting and retaining talent, often tailored to industry standards and individual performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'compensation' generally implies financial remuneration, it can also encompass non-monetary benefits like stock options or flexible working conditions.

vocabulary.definition: Especially is an adverb used to indicate that something is particularly significant or noteworthy in a specific context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, 'especially' is often used to highlight key points or exceptional cases that warrant attention or consideration.
vocabulary.nuance: The use of 'especially' can add emphasis and urgency to a statement, but overuse may dilute its impact.

text: So I was working on parallel things at the same time, and I was often running against the deadline, I was barely finishing it, which is not what I was expecting initially.
speaker: Gergely Orosz
context: Lenny asks about what daily life is like running a newsletter full-time, since people might think writing one post per week sounds easy. Gergely explains that creating quality newsletter content actually takes much more time than expected - requiring research, writing, feedback, and editing phases that can span an entire week. He describes how the first few months were surprisingly stressful as he learned to manage multiple projects simultaneously while working against weekly publishing deadlines.
text_ko: 그래서 저는 여러 일을 동시에 진행하다 보니 자주 마감일에 쫓겨 겨우 끝내곤 했어요. 처음에 기대했던 것과는 달랐어요.
text_zh: 我当时同时在做好几个项目，经常赶deadline，基本上都是卡着点儿完成，这跟我最开始预想的完全不一样。
text_es: Entonces estaba trabajando en varias cosas a la vez, y siempre andaba corriendo contra el tiempo, apenas lograba terminar, que no era para nada lo que esperaba al principio.
key_sentence: I was often running against the deadline, I was barely finishing it, which is not what I was expecting initially.
original_text: So I was working on parallel things at the same time, and I was often running against the deadline, I was barely finishing it, which is not what I was expecting initially. The first few months I feel was a bit more stressed, but again, the good thing is I cleared my calendar, so I said I'm not talking with anyone, I'm just doing this.

vocabulary.definition: Existing or occurring at the same time; similar in nature or function.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and project management, 'parallel' often refers to tasks or projects that are executed simultaneously to optimize time and resources.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'parallel' suggests simultaneous action, it can also imply a need for coordination to ensure that overlapping tasks do not interfere with one another.

vocabulary.definition: A specific date or time by which a task or project must be completed.
vocabulary.businessContext: Deadlines are critical in business settings as they help manage time effectively, ensuring that projects are delivered on schedule and resources are allocated efficiently.
vocabulary.nuance: While deadlines can create urgency and focus, they may also lead to stress if they are perceived as unrealistic or overly tight.

vocabulary.definition: Anticipating or looking forward to a particular outcome or event.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'expecting' often relates to forecasts, projections, or assumptions about future performance or market conditions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a level of uncertainty; it is often used when outcomes are not guaranteed but are hoped for based on available data.

text: Without that, when you're on your own, when you're entrepreneur, I was a great... I think I was a really diligent employee. I always tried to get my work done, show up on time, I tried to meet all expectations.
speaker: Gergely Orosz
context: Gergely and Lenny are discussing the challenges of self-directed work and staying productive without external structure. Gergely shares a surprising discovery about the transition from corporate employment to entrepreneurship - despite being an extremely disciplined and high-performing employee for 15 years, he found himself struggling with productivity and time management when working independently. This illustrates a common challenge entrepreneurs face when they lose the external accountability and structure that corporate environments provide.
text_ko: 그게 없을 때, 혼자 일하거나 창업가로 있을 때는 저는 진짜 성실한 직원이었어요. 항상 일을 제때 끝내려고 하고, 정시에 출근하려고 했으며 모든 기대에 부응하려고 노력했어요.
text_zh: 没有这些的话，当你自己创业的时候，我以前是个很好的...我觉得我是个特别靠谱的员工。我总是努力把活儿干完，按时到岗，尽量达到所有的要求。
text_es: Sin eso, cuando estás por tu cuenta, cuando eres emprendedor... yo era muy... creo que era un empleado muy responsable. Siempre trataba de sacar el trabajo adelante, llegar puntual, cumplir con todo lo que me pedían.
key_sentence: when you're on your own, when you're entrepreneur
original_text: Without that, when you're on your own, when you're entrepreneur, I was a great... I think I was a really diligent employee. I always tried to get my work done, show up on time, I tried to meet all expectations. But what I noticed is, when I started to work for myself, it just went out the window. Almost 15 years of being this star employee who really wants to do well, I found myself upset at myself for not... Just wasting my day.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by steady, earnest, and energetic effort; showing careful and persistent work or effort.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being diligent is crucial for meeting deadlines, maintaining quality standards, and achieving project goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'diligent' conveys a positive work ethic, it can imply a level of meticulousness that may not always be necessary in fast-paced environments.

vocabulary.definition: Beliefs or assumptions about what will happen in the future, often related to performance or outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: Setting clear expectations is vital in business to ensure alignment among team members and to measure success against defined goals.
vocabulary.nuance: Expectations can vary widely among individuals and cultures, so it's important to communicate them clearly to avoid misunderstandings.

text: I use Twitter for a lot of research. And unfortunately what that means is when I start to write something, it can really pull my attention, because I have Twitter open and then I get a message from someone.
speaker: Gergely Orosz
context: Lenny asks Gergely about productivity challenges and how to stay focused while working independently. Gergely describes a specific dilemma many content creators face - Twitter serves a dual purpose as both a research tool and a marketing platform for his newsletter business, making it difficult to avoid distractions. Unlike typical workplace distractions, social media platforms create a complex situation where the distraction source is also legitimately part of the work, making it harder to simply block or avoid.
text_ko: 정보 수집을 위해 트위터를 많이 써요. 그런데 안타깝게도 그게 문제라서, 글을 쓰기 시작하면 트위터를 켜둔 상태에서 누군가 메시지를 보내는 순간 집중이 확 깨져요.
text_zh: 我经常用推特做调研。但问题在于，一旦我开始写东西的时候，注意力就很容易被分散，因为推特一直开着，时不时就会有人发消息过来。
text_es: Uso Twitter para investigar un montón. Y el problema es que cuando me pongo a escribir algo, me distrae muchísimo, porque tengo Twitter abierto y de repente me llega un mensaje de alguien.
key_sentence: it can really pull my attention, because I have Twitter open and then I get a message from someone.
original_text: I use Twitter for a lot of research. And unfortunately what that means is when I start to write something, it can really pull my attention, because I have Twitter open and then I get a message from someone. It's a little bit like Slack, but I'd argue it can be worse, because also Twitter for me is also something that is very useful in generating people raising awareness.

vocabulary.definition: Attention is the cognitive process of selectively concentrating on one aspect of the environment while ignoring other stimuli.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding how to capture and maintain customer attention is vital for marketing strategies and product development.
vocabulary.nuance: Attention can suggest a temporary engagement with a task or subject, and it is often seen as a limited resource that must be managed carefully.

text: And I was asking myself, all right, and then what? And I was like, after I've bought everything that I don't need, I probably want to share what I know with people, do YouTube videos and write books.
speaker: Gergely Orosz
context: Gergely explains his thought process when deciding between starting a traditional venture-funded startup versus pursuing newsletter writing. He was calculating the potential financial outcomes of building a unicorn startup, realizing that even after achieving massive success (like a billion-dollar valuation), his ultimate goal would be to share knowledge through content creation - exactly what he could do immediately. This realization led him to question why he should spend a decade building a company just to end up doing what he was already interested in doing.
text_ko: 그때 스스로 "좋아, 그 다음엔 뭐지?" 하고 물었어요. 그리고 "필요 없는 걸 다 샀으면 아마 내가 아는 걸 사람들과 나누고, 유튜브 영상도 만들고 책도 쓰고 싶을 것 같아요"라고 생각했어요.
text_zh: 我就在想，好吧，然后呢？买完了一堆用不着的东西之后，我可能会想把自己知道的分享给大家，拍拍YouTube视频，写写书什么的。
text_es: Y me preguntaba, bueno, ¿y después qué? Y pensé, después de comprar todo lo que no necesito, probablemente voy a querer compartir lo que sé con la gente, hacer videos de YouTube y escribir libros.
key_sentence: I asked myself, 'and then what?' after buying everything I don't need.
original_text: And I was asking myself, all right, and then what? And I was like, after I've bought everything that I don't need, I probably want to share what I know with people, do YouTube videos and write books. And I was thinking to myself, so hold on. I would go off and do this for like ten years, because that's how much you need to plan to do it.

text: So there was years of work, and I wish I could tell you how to build a successful newsletter, but the best advice I have is still what Jeff Atwood does, except I have less conviction.
speaker: Gergely Orosz
context: Lenny asks how Gergely got his first thousand newsletter subscribers, expecting tactical advice. Gergely explains that his 'overnight success' was actually built on six years of consistent blogging and building an audience. He references advice from Jeff Atwood (Stack Overflow founder) about becoming internet-famous through consistent writing - publish regularly for an extended period. Gergely emphasizes that while he can't guarantee newsletter success, consistent writing practice will definitely improve your skills as a writer.
text_ko: 그 과정에 수년간의 노력이 있었어요. 성공적인 뉴스레터를 어떻게 만드는지 확실히 알려드릴 수 있으면 좋겠지만, 제가 드릴 수 있는 최선의 조언은 여전히 제프 애트우드가 해온 방식이에요. 다만 저한텐 그만큼 확신이 없어요.
text_zh: 这么多年的努力，我真希望能告诉你怎么做出成功的newsletter，但我能给的最好建议还是学Jeff Atwood那套做法，只不过我没他那么有信心。
text_es: Fueron años de trabajo, y me encantaría poder decirte la fórmula para crear un newsletter exitoso, pero el mejor consejo que tengo sigue siendo lo que hace Jeff Atwood, aunque yo lo tengo menos claro.
original_text: So there was years of work, and I wish I could tell you how to build a successful newsletter, but the best advice I have is still what Jeff Atwood does, except I have less conviction. But if you start writing, and you do it regularly, two things will happen. First of all, you're going to you write for yourself and you keep improving, you'll be a better writer. That's for sure.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving desired aims or attaining prosperity and accomplishment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, a successful venture often refers to one that meets its financial goals, scales effectively, and satisfies customer needs.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can vary in meaning based on individual goals; what is deemed successful for one entity may not be for another.

vocabulary.definition: A firmly held belief or opinion, often accompanied by a strong sense of certainty.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, conviction can drive decision-making and influence others, particularly in leadership roles or during negotiations.
vocabulary.nuance: While conviction can inspire confidence, excessive conviction without flexibility may lead to poor decision-making.

vocabulary.definition: Guidance or recommendations concerning prudent future action, typically offered by someone knowledgeable.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business realm, advice is often sought from mentors, consultants, or industry experts to inform strategic decisions and improve operations.
vocabulary.nuance: Advice can be subjective and may vary in relevance depending on the context and the advisor's experience.
